subject: FinTrust DPA: detailed processing partner inventory and cross-border transit appendix
messages:
From: Marco Russo <marco@fintrust.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@fintrust.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: full processing partner inventory + transit details for DPA review

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — as part of our DPA review we need a complete inventory of all processing partners Redwood uses for customer data processing. Specifically FinTrust needs:

- Role (e.g., telemetry, analytics, observability, caching, CDN, KMS/HSM, backups) for each partner
- Countries where customer data is or may be processed (including transient hops)
- Whether any partner holds encryption keys or has access to unencrypted customer data (KMS/HSM details)
- Any planned near-term changes (additions/removals) and expected dates

We also need a short attestation from Redwood regarding whether any of these processors operate in jurisdictions subject to export restrictions, and a copy of any KMS/HSM attestation or SOC2 evidence you can provide.

Can you share a spreadsheet with these columns and indicate which partners are used only for ephemeral transit (e.g., CDN edge) versus long-term storage/processing? We are aiming to close the review by 2027-07-02 so an initial deliverable by EOD Wednesday 2027-06-23 would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Marco
Marco Russo
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Third-Party Risk
FinTrust Bank

Hi Marco —

Appreciate the clear list. I'm attaching a first-pass inventory that maps vendor roles and the primary countries where processing occurs. A few important notes up front:

- The attached spreadsheet is a working export and includes columns for role, primary jurisdiction, transient-country-hops, and whether the vendor has any access to plaintext data.
- For KMS/HSM we currently use a mix of cloud KMS in the US and a third-party HSM provider with roots in EU/US; I flagged those rows in the sheet.
- Transit partners (CDNs, edge proxies) are marked as "ephemeral transit" — they do not persist customer data beyond short caches, but they may route traffic through multiple PoPs.

Attachment: redwood_processing_partners_inventory_20270620_draft.xlsx (see tab "summary" for top-level)

I will loop in Kim (legal) and Marissa (procurement) to finalize the KMS attestation and to prepare any supporting evidence (SOC2 section pointers, encryption architecture diagram). If you can confirm which data categories FinTrust is most concerned with (logs vs. customer payloads vs. telemetry), we can prioritize rows.

Suggested next step: 30-minute sync early next week to walk through the appendix and surface any gaps. When's best for you?

Best,

Hi Marco —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the updated materials we discussed:

- redwood_processing_partners_inventory_20270622.xlsx (tabs: summary, full_roster, kms_hsm_flags)
- transit_paths_appendix.pdf (simple flow diagrams, callouts for ephemeral PoPs vs. persistent processors)

Key points summary:
- Vendors that may touch customer payloads are explicitly marked (column: "data_category_touch"). Non-persistent edge/CDN caches are flagged as "ephemeral transit" and do not store data beyond short TTLs.
- KMS/HSM: primary KMS keys are hosted in AWS KMS (us-east-1) for hosted customers by default. For customers requiring onshore-only key custody we support BYOK and can onboard an HSM escrow option — the vendor that provides HSM attestation is listed and the attestation pdf is available on request.
- Export controls/critical jurisdictions: rows with potential export jurisdiction exposure are flagged in the "jurisdiction_risk" column; none of our persistent storage partners are located in jurisdictions on FinTrust's blocked list per our last procurement sweep.

Next steps: happy to join a 30-minute call to walk through the file and answer questions. I can do 2027-06-24 between 10:00-13:00 PT or 2027-06-25 08:00-11:00 PT — let me know what works for your team.
